INDEPENDENT CONDITIONAL THRESHOLD WRAPPER FROM H_B
================================================

Scope and status
----------------
This is an independent scalar proof from the parent-supplied named premise H_B.
No Cycle10 Luna threshold-wrapper body has been read. H_B is a conditional
premise here; this file does not acquire H_B for any quantum strategy class.
The conclusion applies to finite commuting repeated-game strategies precisely
when H_B holds for every such strategy, every repetition length, and the legal
tensor-product strategies constructed in Section 6. Logarithms are natural.

1. Exact game and conditional premise
------------------------------------
Let G be a finite binary-win two-player game, with finite nonempty answer sets
A and B, a question distribution pi, and commuting value v in [0,1]. Repetition
G^n uses n independent samples from pi. A strategy for the whole repeated game
can correlate all n answers on either player's side. Let W_i in {0,1} be its
actual win indicators and W=sum_i W_i. We assume no independence of these W_i.
Set d=|A||B| and ell=ln d. The game's binary predicate may equivalently include
independent evaluator randomness in the question sample.

For C subset [n], let E_C={W_i=1 for every i in C}, p_C=Pr(E_C), and, only when
p_C>0 and |C|<n, set

  q_C= E[(W-|C|)/(n-|C|) | E_C].

The permitted premise is the following uniform statement, with a fixed B>=1:

  (H_B) q_C <= v+B*((ln(1/p_C)+|C|ell)/(n-|C|))^(1/4).

It holds for every finite commuting repeated-game strategy, every integer n>=1,
and every proper C with p_C>0. In particular C=empty has p_C=1 and q_C=EW/n<=v.
No convention for q_C is required when p_C=0. The premise is required for all
strategies, not just a particular strategy or its own conditional extensions.

2. Exact all-n theorem
---------------------
Under H_B, for every legal strategy, every n>=1, and every

  0<delta<=1-v,

one has, with the explicit positive constant c_B=1/(1024 B^4),

  Pr[W >= ceil((v+delta)n)]
    <= exp[-c_B*delta^5*n/(delta+ell)].                  (2.1)

For d=1 the denominator is delta and (2.1) means exp[-c_B delta^4 n].

CYCLE 10 — REPETITION LOWER-BOUND AUDIT
Independent literature review; 2026-10-09

STATUS
This report audits lower-bound obstructions to the proposed conditional consequences. It does not establish either proposed upper bound. It does not inspect the active sampler, bridge, or wrapper proof bodies.

MAIN RESULT
The strongest model-matched obstruction found is the Kempe–Regev binary line game. It has answer-product size d=4 and exact commuting one-round gap epsilon_m=1/(2m-1). For every repetition count ell >= m^2, its repeated commuting value is at least (1-O(m^-2))^ell. Since m^-2=Theta(epsilon_m^2), no universal all-wins exponent f(epsilon,d) can satisfy f(epsilon,4)/epsilon^2 -> infinity as epsilon -> 0. In particular, a general fixed-alphabet rate proportional to epsilon, or epsilon^p for any p<2, is impossible. The proposed epsilon^3/(epsilon+log d) rate is consistent with this obstruction and has room for one epsilon power of improvement at fixed d; the audit does not prove that improvement.

1. EXACT COMMUTING-MODEL OBSTRUCTION: THE LINE GAME

For integer m>=2, the line game L_m has questions [m] for each player and answer alphabets {1,2}. The verifier chooses uniformly one of the 2m-1 edges of the path with vertices 1,...,m, including one loop at each vertex. All constraints require equal answers except the loop at vertex 1, which forces both answers to 1, and the loop at vertex m, which forces both answers to 2. Thus d=|A||B|=4.

Kempe–Regev, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, prove
  omega(L_m) = omega_tensor(L_m) = omega_ns(L_m) = 1 - 1/(2m-1).
Here omega is the classical value, omega_tensor is the shared-entanglement/tensor value, and omega_ns is the no-signaling value. Every tensor strategy is a commuting strategy, and every commuting strategy is no-signaling: for commuting measurement effects A_a^x and B_b^y, summing over b gives the Alice marginal <psi|A_a^x|psi>, independent of y. Hence
  omega_tensor(L_m) <= omega_co(L_m) <= omega_ns(L_m),
so the commuting value is also exactly 1-1/(2m-1), with epsilon_m=1/(2m-1).

For the conventional ell-fold parallel product, each coordinate's question edge is sampled independently from this same law; Alice and Bob receive their full question vectors simultaneously, return answer vectors, and the verifier accepts iff every coordinate constraint is satisfied.
